lesson_title: Eggs in an Egg Box: Why Volume Division Lies
hook_text: Box volume ÷ jar volume = the WRONG answer. Every time. Here's the count that works.
clip_script: Fitting jars into a box is the egg-box problem. Nobody pours eggs into a box and hopes; the box has spots. Jars of diameter 8 in a box 32 long: four spots. Across the 24 width: three. The floor is a grid of 4 by 3 — 12 spots. Box 10 high, jar 10 tall: one storey. Twelve jars. Never divide volumes — the clever-sounding shortcut overcounts, because jars are round and boxes are square: the corners around every jar are dead air that liquid maths would happily fill. And if the box were 35 long? Still 4 jars — the spare 3 centimetres holds nothing. Fitting rounds DOWN. Count spots, not space.
visual_style: Top-down box grid filling with jars one row at a time, corner gaps flashing red as a ghostly 'volume answer' jar tries to squeeze in and bounces out.
pacing: Rhythmic row-by-row fill, one comic rejection beat, crisp rule stated at the end.
